picks.title: Unity-Based Algorithm For Seamless Dungeon Generation
picks.excerpt: A developer shared the Labyrinth Procedural Generator, a Unity algorithm that stitches dungeon rooms into seamless, playable layouts, with a live demo to try. Learn how the Labyrinth Procedural Generator works and try the demo.
picks.rationale: Concrete, try-it-today procedural level design in Unity — shows exactly what generation buys a level designer versus hand-authored layout, and where the seams still need human design.

picks.title: Unity's Stylized Water 3 Is Getting Spline-Based River Modeler Tool
picks.excerpt: Stylized Water 3 is adding a spline-driven river modeler for Unity. It's designed around Burst and the Job System, features segmented river output, and automatic VFX/SFX integration.
picks.rationale: Procedural authoring the artist still steers: the spline is the control surface, a useful counterpoint to prompt-first environment generation, with Burst/Job System performance baked in.

picks.title: The AI paradox: why mobile embraces AI and triple-A holds back
picks.excerpt: At PGC Summit Shanghai, studio leaders and investors asked why free-to-play races to adopt AI while AAA holds back, tracing the split to production risk and audience expectation.
picks.rationale: Explains the split adoption curve by production model rather than ideology — a usable frame for any design org deciding how fast to move, and distinct from the Nordic-studios piece already published on 08-26.

picks.title: DDoS Attack Breaks Beloved Video Game Wiki After AI Bro Was Banned
picks.excerpt: The Cutting Room Floor wiki went offline after a DDoS attack allegedly triggered by a contributor banned for using Claude Code. The site had already deployed anti-AI defenses, including MS Paint warnings served to scrapers.
picks.rationale: Game-history archives are hardening against AI agents and scrapers — the reference material designers and researchers rely on is becoming a contested, actively defended resource.

picks.title: Twitch faces a class action lawsuit over using streamers' content to train Amazon's AI
picks.excerpt: Twitch content creator Warren Pandiscia has filed a proposed class action against Twitch and Amazon, alleging the companies used streamers' content to train AI.
picks.rationale: Creator-made game content used as training data without consent — the platform-rights fight that lands on anyone whose work lives on infrastructure they do not own.
